rtxremix.hotkey.header: Hotkeys (click a button, then press a key; Delete clears)
rtxremix.setting.light.fix.tip: Master switch for ALL of the light transform modifications: glass light tint, saturation, pane depth, water fixes and sun size. Off = the original shipped rendering exactly, whatever the sliders below say; they keep their values for when you turn it back on. Hotkey: Numpad 1.
rtxremix.setting.light.debugMarkers.tip: Needs the diagnostic shader build. Light that crosses glass is drawn red on shadow rays and green on bounce rays. Off by default. Hotkey: Numpad 2.
rtxremix.setting.light.saturation.tip: Scales how saturated the tint of stained glass is for light passing through it (shadow rays and bounce rays). 100 = the glass colours as shipped, 25 = mostly grey, 200 = twice as saturated. Only applies while the Glass Light Fix is on.
rtxremix.setting.light.paneDepth.tip: How strongly a stained glass pane tints what you see through it when you look straight at it. Panes are thin, so by default they show only a pale part of their colour. 0 = the original look, 100 = the pane shows its full colour, 150 = deeper, 280 = as deep as a glass block. Glass blocks are not changed. Only applies while the Glass Light Fix is on.
rtxremix.setting.light.glassDepth.tip: How strongly a thick glass block tints what you see and the light that passes through it. 100 = as shipped, 200 = the colour is squared (twice as deep), 75 = lighter. It changes the glass material itself, so it applies after the glass materials are rebuilt: reload resources (F3+T) or restart the game. Panes use the Glass Pane Depth Effect instead.
rtxremix.setting.light.waterBlue.tip: How much blue light water lets through. 100 = as shipped (red 0.6, green 0.9, blue 0.89 per metre: cyan). Lower = less blue, so the water leans green and teal, higher = bluer. It changes the water material itself, so it applies after the materials are rebuilt: reload resources (F3+T) or restart the game.
rtxremix.setting.light.glassGap.tip: Separates glass blocks that touch each other (different colours of glass, glass against water) by a hairline of air, so the faces between them are no longer on the same plane. Fixes the sky going black behind two different glasses, middle glass blocks missing from the colour mix, and glass under water flickering. The terrain rebuilds when you change it.
rtxremix.setting.light.waterUnderside.ti: Test switch. Keeps the downward-facing copy of the water's top surface, so a view ray that comes up through water (for example from inside a glass room under a lake) can leave it and see the sky. Off = the fix's default, which removes that copy. The terrain rebuilds when you change it.
rtxremix.setting.light.waterNudge.tip: Test switch. Pulls the faces of water that touch glass a hair away from the glass, so the glass and the water are never exactly on the same surface and a view ray crosses them in a defined order (this is what can make the sky behind glass and water render dark). The terrain rebuilds when you change it.
rtxremix.setting.light.sunSize.tip: How big the sun and moon appear, in percent of the real size (100 = the shipped size). A bigger sun gives softer, wider shadow edges, for example under a cube; the real sun gives very sharp shadows at this scale. Applies while the Glass Light Fix is on.
rtxremix.setting.light.hotkeys.tip: Allow the hotkeys below. Click a key button, then press the key you want (Delete clears it). Defaults: Numpad 1 master switch, Numpad 2 debug markers. The same keys are listed in Controls.
